models.name: hrm_platform_guests
models.description:
Temporary guest accounts for unauthenticated visitors to the platform.

Guests are anonymous users who have not yet logged in or established any identity with the system. Each guest is identified by a device fingerprint rather than a persistent user account. This table tracks guest access for security monitoring purposes while maintaining complete data isolation from organizational content.

Key characteristics:
- Stateless access with no session persistence
- No organization context or personalization
- Identified solely by device fingerprint
- Used for security monitoring and access attempt logging

Related entities:
- {@link hrm_platform_guest_sessions} - Temporary session tokens for guest access

plainFields.name: device_fingerprint
plainFields.description: Unique device identifier used to recognize returning guest visitors. Generated from browser/device characteristics for fingerprinting purposes.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which the guest accessed the platform. Used for security monitoring and access pattern analysis.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser and device user agent string from the guest's request. Used for device identification and security analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest record was first created upon initial access.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest record was soft deleted. Used for retention policy enforcement and cleanup.

models.name: hrm_platform_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest access without persistent authentication.

This table tracks short-lived session tokens for guest users during authentication flows such as sign-up or login processes. Unlike member or admin sessions, guest sessions are temporary and do not persist across requests.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_platform_guests} - Links to the guest actor record
- Stores connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) for security monitoring
- Tracks session lifecycle with created_at and expired_at timestamps

Important notes:
- Guest sessions are typically short-lived and do not provide persistent authentication
- Used during transitional states before full user authentication
- Session tokens are not cached and each request is evaluated independently
- All guest access attempts are logged for security monitoring purposes

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_guest_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged guest's {@link hrm_platform_guests.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the guest during session creation for security monitoring.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL where the guest initiated the session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The referrer URL that led the guest to the current page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the guest session expires. Used for session lifecycle management and security.

models.name: hrm_platform_members
models.description:
Registered member accounts with email/password authentication credentials.

Members are authenticated users who can access the platform and perform actions within their assigned role permissions. Each member has a unique email address for authentication and can belong to multiple organizations through employee relationships (managed in {@link hrm_platform_employees}).

Key characteristics:
- Serves as the primary identity record for member actors
- Owns authentication credentials (email and password hash)
- Has one-to-many sessions stored in {@link hrm_platform_member_sessions}
- Can have multiple employee records across different organizations
- Supports soft deletion for account deactivation without data loss

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for member authentication and account identification.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password for secure authentication. Never stores plain text passwords.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the member account was soft-deleted. Null indicates active account.

models.name: hrm_platform_member_sessions
models.description: JWT session tokens for member authentication with organization context. Each session represents an active login for a member account, tracking the authenticated member, their current organization context, connection details (IP, href, referrer), and session lifecycle (created_at, expired_at). Members can switch between organizations they belong to, and this table tracks which organization is currently active for the session.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the authenticated member account. {@link hrm_platform_members.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Current active organization for this session. Members can switch contexts. {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address where the session was initiated from.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL where the session was initiated from.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The referrer URL from the HTTP request that created this session.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session was created upon successful authentication.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this session expires or was explicitly logged out.

models.name: hrm_platform_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for member account recovery.

This table stores temporary tokens generated when a member requests a password reset. Each token is unique, has an expiration time, and can only be used once. When a member clicks the password reset link in their email, the system validates the token against this table before allowing the password change.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_platform_members} - each reset request is associated with a specific member account
- Tokens are generated with sufficient entropy to prevent guessing
- Expired or used tokens are automatically invalidated

Business context:
- Supports the password recovery workflow defined in the authentication requirements
- Tokens typically expire within 1-24 hours for security
- Once used, tokens cannot be reused even if not expired
- Multiple tokens may exist for the same member if they request multiple resets

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_member_id
foreignFields.description: Associated member's {@link hrm_platform_members.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique password reset token with sufficient entropy for security.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reset token expires and becomes invalid.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this reset token was used. Null if token has not been used yet.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset request was created.

models.name: hrm_platform_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for member account registration confirmation.

This table stores time-limited, single-use tokens that are sent to members via email for account verification during the registration process. Each verification record is linked to a specific member account and includes an expiration timestamp to ensure tokens are time-bound. The table supports account security by enabling one-time use validation and optional IP/user-agent tracking for audit purposes.

**Key relationships**:
- Links to {@link hrm_platform_members} via foreign key
- One-to-many relationship (one member can have multiple verification attempts)
- Supports re-verification workflows

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_member_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the member account being verified. {@link hrm_platform_members.id}

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique verification token code sent to member email for validation.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token expires.

plainFields.name: used
plainFields.description: Whether this token has already been used for verification.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the device that requested this verification.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: User agent string of the device that requested this verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification token was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft deletion if applicable.

models.name: hrm_platform_admins
models.description:
Administrator accounts with email/password authentication and elevated privileges for organization management.

Administrators are authenticated users who possess elevated privileges to manage organization settings, employees, roles, departments, projects, tasks, and timesheet approvals within their assigned organizations. Each admin account has unique email credentials and can belong to multiple organizations with varying permission levels.

Key relationships:
- Has many {@link hrm_platform_admin_sessions} for active authentication sessions
- Has many {@link hrm_platform_admin_password_resets} for password recovery tokens
- Belongs to multiple {@link hrm_platform_organizations} through session context
- Can manage {@link hrm_platform_employees}, {@link hrm_platform_projects}, {@link hrm_platform_tasks} within organization scope

Important behavioral notes:
- Admin authentication is separate from member authentication for security isolation
- Admin accounts can be soft-deleted but credentials remain for audit trail
- Email addresses must be unique across all admin accounts
- Admin privileges are organization-scoped and cannot cross multi-tenancy boundaries

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for administrator authentication and identification.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: BCrypt hashed password for secure administrator authentication.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator account was soft-deleted. Null indicates active account.

models.name: hrm_platform_admin_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for administrator authentication with elevated access within organizations.

This table maintains the authenticated state of administrator users who possess elevated privileges across their organization. Each session is scoped to a specific administrator account and preserves connection metadata for security auditing.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to a single {@link hrm_platform_admins} administrator account
- Sessions are append-only and represent login events
- Multiple concurrent sessions allowed per administrator across different devices

Behavioral notes:
- Sessions persist until administrator logs out, account is deleted, or organization is removed
- Session termination occurs immediately upon logout action
- All session actions are recorded in {@link hrm_platform_activity_logs} for audit purposes
- Administrators can maintain concurrent sessions within the same organization
- Sessions do not implement automatic expiration based on time or inactivity

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged administrator's {@link hrm_platform_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the device used for administrator login.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL where the administrator initiated the login session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that directed the administrator to the login page.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator session was created upon successful login.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator session was terminated through logout or system action.

models.name: hrm_platform_admin_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrator account recovery.

This table stores one-time use tokens that allow administrators to reset their passwords when they have lost access to their account. Each token is associated with a specific administrator account and has an expiration time for security purposes.

Key characteristics:

- Tokens are generated when an administrator requests a password reset
- Each token can only be used once (tracked via used_at timestamp)
- Tokens expire after a configured time period (typically 1-24 hours)
- Multiple tokens can exist for the same administrator (e.g., if they request multiple resets)
- Used tokens are not deleted immediately for audit trail purposes

Relationships:

- Belongs to {@link hrm_platform_admins} - Links to the administrator account requesting the reset
- One-to-many relationship: One admin can have multiple password reset tokens over time

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged administrator's {@link hrm_platform_admins.id}. Links the password reset token to the administrator account requesting the reset.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: The password reset token string. This is a cryptographically secure random string that the administrator uses to verify their identity when resetting their password. The token is sent to the administrator's registered email address.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was generated. Used to calculate token age and determine if the token has expired.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token expires. Tokens are invalid after this time for security purposes. Typically set to 1-24 hours after creation.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was used to reset the password. Null if the token has not been used yet. Once set, the token cannot be used again.

models.name: hrm_platform_organizations
models.description:
Main organization records representing the primary business container within the platform.

Organizations serve as the fundamental multi-tenancy boundary, ensuring complete data isolation between different companies or business units using the platform. Each organization contains employees, projects, tasks, time tracking data, and all business operations scoped to that organization.

Key characteristics:
- Unique name identifies the organization across the system
- Owner reference tracks which member created and controls the organization
- Soft delete support allows organization deactivation while preserving data integrity
- All organization-scoped entities reference this table for multi-tenancy enforcement

Related entities:
- {@link hrm_platform_organization_settings} stores organization-specific configuration (currency, timezone, fiscal year)
- {@link hrm_platform_organization_logos} stores branding assets
- {@link hrm_platform_employees} belong to organizations
- {@link hrm_platform_projects} belong to organizations
- {@link hrm_platform_departments} belong to organizations

foreignFields.name: owner_id
foreignFields.description: Owner's {@link hrm_platform_members.id}. The member who created and has full control over this organization.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Organization name, must be unique across the system.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description providing additional context about the organization's purpose or structure.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was soft deleted. NULL means organization is active.

models.name: hrm_platform_organization_settings
models.description:
Organization-specific configuration settings including currency, timezone, and fiscal year parameters.

This table stores operational settings that define how an organization manages its business operations. Each organization has exactly one settings record that controls:

- **Currency**: The default currency code for financial calculations and reporting
- **Timezone**: The organization's primary timezone for timestamp display and scheduling
- **Fiscal Year Start Month**: The month (1-12) when the organization's fiscal year begins

These settings are subsidiary to the {@link hrm_platform_organizations} entity and are managed through organization administration workflows. Changes to settings affect all organization-scoped operations including time tracking, reporting, and financial calculations.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged organization's {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}. Each organization has exactly one settings record.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Three-letter ISO currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'KRW') for financial calculations and reporting within the organization.

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description: IANA timezone identifier (e.g., 'Asia/Seoul', 'America/New_York') for timestamp display and scheduling operations.

plainFields.name: fiscal_year_start_month
plainFields.description: The month number (1-12) when the organization's fiscal year begins. Used for financial reporting and period calculations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization settings record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization settings were last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization settings were soft-deleted. Null indicates active settings.

models.name: hrm_platform_organization_logos
models.description:
Logo images and branding assets for organizations.

This table stores logo image references for organizations to provide visual identification in the user interface. Each organization can have at most one active logo, establishing a 1:1 relationship with {@link hrm_platform_organizations}.

The logo is managed through the parent organization entity and is not independently searchable or filterable. When an organization is deleted, its logo is also removed through cascade deletion.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to exactly one {@link hrm_platform_organizations} (1:1 relationship)

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged organization's {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}. Establishes 1:1 relationship where each organization has at most one logo.

plainFields.name: image_url
plainFields.description: URL or path to the logo image file. Stores the location of the uploaded logo image for display in the user interface.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the logo was uploaded/created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the logo was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the logo was soft deleted. Null indicates the logo is currently active.

models.name: hrm_platform_employees
models.description:
Employee records that establish work relationships between users and organizations.

This table represents an individual's working relationship within a specific organization, creating a bridge between a user account and organization-specific work responsibilities. Each employee record enables the individual to participate in organizational activities including time tracking, project work, and timesheet submission.

Key relationships:
- Links to {@link hrm_platform_members} for user authentication and identity
- Belongs to {@link hrm_platform_organizations} establishing organizational context
- Optionally assigned to {@link hrm_platform_departments} for organizational grouping
- Assigned exactly one {@link hrm_platform_roles} determining permissions and authorization

Business rules:
- Employment type classification: full-time, part-time, contractor, or intern
- Status tracking: active employees can log time and submit timesheets; deactivated employees cannot create new entries but historical data is preserved
- Each user can have multiple employee records across different organizations
- Role assignment determines what actions the employee can perform within the organization

foreignFields.name: member_id
foreignFields.description: User account that this employee record represents. Links to the authenticated member identity. {@link hrm_platform_members.id}

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization where this employee works. Establishes the organizational context for all employee activities. {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: department_id
foreignFields.description: Department assignment for organizational grouping. Optional field that can be null if employee is not assigned to any department. When department is deleted, this is set to null. {@link hrm_platform_departments.id}

foreignFields.name: role_id
foreignFields.description: Role assigned to this employee determining permissions and authorization level. Each employee must have exactly one role. {@link hrm_platform_roles.id}

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description: Classification of the employment relationship. Valid values: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern. Determines how the employee's work is tracked and reported.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current employment status. Valid values: active, deactivated. Active employees can log time and submit timesheets. Deactivated employees cannot create new entries but historical data is preserved.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this employee record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this employee record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this employee record was soft-deleted. Null means the record is active. Used for reactivation support.

models.name: hrm_platform_roles
models.description:
Role definitions within organizations for role-based access control.

Roles represent named collections of permissions that determine what actions employees can perform within an organization. Each role aggregates specific permissions defining capabilities such as managing employees, viewing projects, approving timesheets, or accessing reports.

The system includes three built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) that cannot be deleted or modified, providing a standard permission structure. Organization owners can also create custom roles with tailored permission combinations to match specific job functions.

Each employee is assigned exactly one role, which determines their authorization level. When a role is assigned to an employee, they inherit all permissions associated with that role.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_platform_organizations} - roles are scoped to specific organizations
- Assigned to many {@link hrm_platform_employees} - employees reference their assigned role
- Maps to many permissions through {@link hrm_platform_role_permissions} - junction table for role-based access control

Built-in roles (is_builtin = true) cannot be deleted under any circumstances. Custom roles (is_builtin = false) can only be deleted if no employees are currently assigned to them.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged organization's {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}. Roles are scoped to specific organizations and cannot be shared across organizations.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique name of the role within the organization. Built-in roles have predefined names: 'Owner', 'Manager', 'Employee'. Custom roles can have any descriptive name chosen by the organization owner.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description explaining the role's purpose and typical responsibilities. Helps administrators understand what the role is intended for when assigning employees.

plainFields.name: is_builtin
plainFields.description: Whether this is a built-in role (Owner, Manager, Employee) or a custom role. Built-in roles cannot be deleted or modified. Custom roles can be deleted if no employees are assigned.

plainFields.name: built_in_type
plainFields.description: Type identifier for built-in roles: 'owner', 'manager', or 'employee'. NULL for custom roles. Used to identify and protect built-in roles from deletion or modification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the role was created. Built-in roles are created during organization setup. Custom roles are created when organization owners define new permission combinations.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the role was last modified. Custom roles can be updated to change name, description, or permissions. Built-in roles should rarely be updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the role was soft-deleted. Only custom roles can be deleted. Built-in roles cannot be deleted. When deleted, the role is no longer available for new employee assignments.

models.name: hrm_platform_departments
models.description: Departmental organizational units within organizations that provide structural grouping for employees. Departments support a one-level hierarchical structure where a department can have one parent department, enabling subdepartment organization. Each department belongs to exactly one organization and must have a unique name within that organization. Departments facilitate employee assignment and organizational reporting structures.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_organization_id
foreignFields.description: The organization that owns this department. {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Optional parent department for one-level hierarchy. Only one level of nesting is supported.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Unique name identifying the department within its organization.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description clarifying the department's business purpose and responsibilities.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the department was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for department deactivation.

models.name: hrm_platform_employee_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of employee records for audit trail and historical tracking.

This table captures the complete state of employee records at specific moments in time, preserving historical data for compliance, auditing, and recovery purposes. Each snapshot contains all employee attributes denormalized, including employment classification, status, department assignment, and role association.

Key characteristics:
- Append-only: Snapshots are created but never modified or deleted
- Denormalized: All employee data is captured at snapshot time, independent of future changes to referenced entities
- Historical preservation: Maintains accurate record of employee state even if related entities (departments, roles) are later modified or deleted
- Audit trail: Enables tracking of employee record changes over time

Relationships:
- {@link hrm_platform_employees} - One snapshot per employee record change (1:1 via unique constraint)
- {@link hrm_platform_organizations} - Organization context at snapshot time
- {@link hrm_platform_members} - User identity at snapshot time
- {@link hrm_platform_departments} - Department assignment at snapshot time (nullable)
- {@link hrm_platform_roles} - Role assignment at snapshot time

foreignFields.name: employees_id
foreignFields.description: Referenced employee record's {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}. Each snapshot corresponds to exactly one employee record change.

foreignFields.name: organizations_id
foreignFields.description: Organization's {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id} where the employee works, captured at snapshot time.

foreignFields.name: members_id
foreignFields.description: User's {@link hrm_platform_members.id} associated with this employee record, captured at snapshot time.

foreignFields.name: departments_id
foreignFields.description: Department's {@link hrm_platform_departments.id} where the employee is assigned, captured at snapshot time. Nullable if employee had no department assignment.

foreignFields.name: roles_id
foreignFields.description: Role's {@link hrm_platform_roles.id} assigned to the employee, captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description: Employment classification at snapshot time. Valid values: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Employee status at snapshot time. Valid values: active, deactivated.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: employee_created_at
plainFields.description: Original employee record creation timestamp, captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: employee_updated_at
plainFields.description: Employee record last update timestamp, captured at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: employee_deleted_at
plainFields.description: Employee record deletion timestamp, captured at snapshot time. Nullable if employee was not deleted.

models.name: hrm_platform_employee_invitations
models.description:
Tracks pending employee invitations sent by managers to potential new hires. Stores the invitee's email, assigned role, target organization, invitation status, and unique redemption token. Used in the employee onboarding workflow where managers invite people to join the organization.

This table exists independently of employee records since invitations are sent before employee relationships are established. Once an invitation is redeemed, the user creates an account and an employee record is subsequently created linking them to the organization.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged organization's {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_role_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned role's {@link hrm_platform_roles.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_member_id
foreignFields.description: User who redeemed the invitation's {@link hrm_platform_members.id}

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Email address of the person being invited to join the organization.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique secure token for invitation redemption.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the invitation (pending, accepted, expired, revoked).

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp after which the invitation is no longer valid.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was last updated.

plainFields.name: redeemed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was accepted by the invitee.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was soft deleted. Null means the invitation is active.

models.name: hrm_platform_role_permissions
models.description:
Junction table mapping roles to their granted permissions for role-based access control.

This table establishes the many-to-many relationship between {@link hrm_platform_roles} and permission codes. Each record represents a single permission granted to a specific role.

**Business Context**:

Roles in the system (both built-in and custom) are defined by the set of permissions they grant. This table stores those permission assignments, enabling flexible role-based access control.

**Available Permissions** (from Section 57):

- Organization management: edit organization settings
- Employee management: add, edit, or deactivate employees
- Employee viewing: view employee list and details
- Project management: create, edit, delete projects and tasks
- Project viewing: view projects and tasks
- Time management: edit or delete any employee's timelogs
- Time approval: approve or reject timesheets
- Time viewing: view all employees' timelogs and timesheets
- Report viewing: view organization reports

**Key Constraints**:

- Each role can have a permission only once (enforced by unique index)
- Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) have pre-configured permissions
- Custom roles can be assigned any combination of available permissions
- Soft delete support via deleted_at field for audit trail and recovery

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_role_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged role's {@link hrm_platform_roles.id}. This foreign key links the permission to the role that grants it.

plainFields.name: permission_code
plainFields.description: Permission identifier string that defines a specific capability. Examples include 'organization_edit', 'employee_manage', 'employee_view', 'project_manage', 'project_view', 'time_manage', 'time_approve', 'time_view', 'report_view'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission was granted to the role.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission assignment was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this permission assignment was soft deleted. Null indicates the permission is currently active.

models.name: hrm_platform_contracts
models.description:
Employment agreements between organizations and employees with compensation terms, pay periods, and working hours.

Each contract represents a formal employment agreement that establishes the specific terms under which an employee works for an organization. Contracts define compensation rates, payment frequency, and working hour expectations.

Key relationships:
- Each contract belongs to exactly one {@link hrm_platform_employees} and cannot exist independently of an employee record
- Each contract belongs to exactly one {@link hrm_platform_organizations} for multi-tenancy data isolation
- Multiple contracts can exist for a single employee over their employment history, but only one contract can be active at any given time
- Active contracts are those without an end_at date or with an end_at in the future
- Historical contracts (with end_at in the past) become immutable records for compliance and auditing

Contract versioning ensures continuous coverage without gaps: when a new contract is created, the previous active contract is automatically ended by setting its end_at to the day before the new contract starts.

This table is referenced by {@link hrm_platform_contract_snapshots} for audit trail preservation.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged employee's {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}. Each contract is tied to a specific employee and cannot exist independently.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged organization's {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}. Ensures multi-tenancy data isolation.

plainFields.name: start_at
plainFields.description: The date when the employment terms begin. Required field that marks the start of the contract.

plainFields.name: end_at
plainFields.description: The date when the employment terms conclude. Optional field - when null, the contract is considered ongoing and continues indefinitely. When present, must be on or after start_at.

plainFields.name: pay_rate
plainFields.description: The employee's compensation amount expressed in the organization's configured currency. Represents the base compensation before any deductions or additional benefits.

plainFields.name: pay_period
plainFields.description: The frequency of payment cycles. One of: hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly. Determines how the pay_rate is interpreted in compensation calculations.

plainFields.name: working_hours_per_week
plainFields.description: The standard working hours per week for the employee. Establishes the expected full-time equivalent baseline for calculating overtime, part-time ratios, and workload expectations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this contract was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this contract was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this contract was soft deleted. Null indicates the contract is active in the system.

models.name: hrm_platform_contract_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of contract records for audit trail and historical tracking.

This table captures the complete state of employment contracts at specific moments in time, enabling:

- **Audit Trail**: Track all changes to contract terms over time
- **Compliance**: Maintain immutable records of employment agreements for legal requirements
- **Historical Reference**: View what contract terms were in effect at any point in time
- **Recovery**: Restore previous contract states if needed

Each snapshot is created when a contract is modified, preserving the original terms including compensation, pay period, working hours, and duration. Snapshots are immutable once created and serve as the authoritative historical record of employment agreements.

Relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_platform_contracts} - the contract being snapshot
- References {@link hrm_platform_employees} - the employee under contract
- References {@link hrm_platform_organizations} - the organization employing the worker

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_contract_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the contract being snapshot. {@link hrm_platform_contracts.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the employee under this contract. {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the organization employing the worker. {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}

plainFields.name: start_at
plainFields.description: The date when this contract employment terms begin. Required field that marks the start of the employment agreement.

plainFields.name: end_at
plainFields.description: The date when this contract employment terms conclude. Optional field - null indicates ongoing contract without end date.

plainFields.name: pay_rate
plainFields.description: The compensation amount specified in the contract. Required numeric value representing base pay before deductions.

plainFields.name: pay_period
plainFields.description: The frequency of payment cycles. One of: hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly. Determines how pay_rate is interpreted.

plainFields.name: working_hours_per_week
plainFields.description: The standard working hours per week for the employee. Required value establishing full-time equivalent baseline for overtime and workload calculations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created. Records the point in time when contract state was captured.

models.name: hrm_platform_projects
models.description:
Work containers within organizations that group related work efforts and business initiatives.

Projects serve as the primary organizational structure for tracking time expenditures against specific business objectives. Each project represents a distinct body of work that employees contribute time and effort towards achieving specific goals.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_platform_organizations} - projects are scoped to a single organization
- Has many {@link hrm_platform_project_memberships} - links employees to projects with role designations
- Has many {@link hrm_platform_tasks} - tasks are discrete work units within projects

Status states:
- `active`: Work is currently in progress, accepting new time entries
- `completed`: All planned work finished, historical records accessible but no new time entries
- `archived`: Preserved for historical reference, read-only for time tracking

Visual identification via color_code enables employees to quickly distinguish between multiple projects when creating time entries or viewing reports.

foreignFields.name: organization_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged organization's {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}. Projects are scoped to a single organization and cannot span multiple organizations.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Required project name that uniquely identifies the project within the organization. Used as the primary identifier for employees when selecting projects for time entries and task assignments.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description that clarifies the project's purpose, scope, and boundaries. Helps employees understand which work belongs to which project when logging time.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Project lifecycle status. Valid values: 'active' (work in progress, accepting time entries), 'completed' (work finished, read-only), 'archived' (historical reference, read-only). Completed and archived projects prevent new time entries.

plainFields.name: color_code
plainFields.description: Required color code for visual distinction across user interfaces. Enables employees to quickly identify projects when creating time entries, viewing reports, or browsing project lists.

plainFields.name: budget_hours
plainFields.description: Optional total estimated effort in hours for the project. Provides a baseline against which actual time logged can be compared to track whether work is proceeding within planned estimates.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was soft deleted. Null indicates the project is active.

models.name: hrm_platform_project_memberships
models.description:
Junction table linking employees to projects with role designations.

This table establishes many-to-many relationships between employees and projects, enabling employees to participate in multiple projects and projects to have multiple team members. Each membership record includes a role designation (member or project-lead) that determines the employee's level of authority within the project.

Key relationships:
- Links to {@link hrm_platform_employees} via foreign key
- Links to {@link hrm_platform_projects} via foreign key
- Each employee can have multiple memberships across different projects
- Each project can have multiple member employees
- Only one membership per employee-project combination (enforced by unique constraint)

Role designations:
- "member": Regular team member with standard project access
- "project-lead": Project lead with elevated permissions for task management and team coordination

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged employee's {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}. Establishes which employee is assigned to the project.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_project_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged project's {@link hrm_platform_projects.id}. Establishes which project the employee is assigned to.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description: Role designation within the project. Valid values are 'member' for regular team members or 'project-lead' for employees with elevated task management permissions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was soft deleted. Null indicates active membership.

models.name: hrm_platform_project_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of project records for audit trail and historical tracking.

These snapshots capture the complete state of a project at specific moments in time, preserving historical data for compliance, recovery, and audit purposes. Each snapshot is immutable once created and reflects the exact state of the project including all denormalized fields.

Key characteristics:
- **Immutable records**: Once created, snapshots are never modified or deleted
- **Complete state capture**: All project fields are denormalized to preserve exact historical state
- **Audit trail**: Enables tracking of project lifecycle changes over time
- **Compliance support**: Provides verifiable historical records for regulatory requirements

Related entities:
- Parent: {@link hrm_platform_projects} - The project being snapshot
- Organization: {@link hrm_platform_organizations} - Organization that owns the project
- Creator: {@link hrm_platform_members} - User who created the snapshot

foreignFields.name: project_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent project record being snapshot. {@link hrm_platform_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization that owns this project snapshot. {@link hrm_platform_organizations.id}

foreignFields.name: created_by_id
foreignFields.description: Member who created this snapshot. {@link hrm_platform_members.id}

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Unique project code within the organization at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Project name at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Project description at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Project status at snapshot time (active, completed, archived).

plainFields.name: color_code
plainFields.description: Visual color identifier for the project at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: budget_hours
plainFields.description: Budgeted hours for the project at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

models.name: hrm_platform_tasks
models.description:
Main task entity representing discrete work units within projects. Tasks are the smallest unit of work tracking with status progression, priority classification, and optional subtask relationships.

Tasks belong to projects and can be assigned to employees who are members of that project. Each task may have an optional parent task for one-level subtask hierarchy (subtasks cannot have their own subtasks). Task status changes are automatically recorded in {@link hrm_platform_task_histories} for audit trail purposes.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to exactly one {@link hrm_platform_projects}
- Optionally assigned to one {@link hrm_platform_employees} (must be project member)
- Optionally has one parent {@link hrm_platform_tasks} (for subtasks)
- Has many child subtasks (through self-referential relationship)
- Has many {@link hrm_platform_task_histories} entries for status change audit
- Has many {@link hrm_platform_task_snapshots} for point-in-time state preservation
- Created by a {@link hrm_platform_members} for audit trail

Tasks support optional due dates for deadline tracking and estimated hours for effort planning. The status field tracks task progression through the workflow lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_project_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged project's {@link hrm_platform_projects.id}. Tasks must belong to exactly one project.

foreignFields.name: assigned_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned employee's {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}. Optional - task may remain unassigned. Employee must be a member of the project containing this task.

foreignFields.name: parent_task_id
foreignFields.description: Parent task's {@link hrm_platform_tasks.id}. Optional - if set, this task is a subtask of the parent. Subtasks cannot have their own subtasks (one level only).

foreignFields.name: created_by_member_id
foreignFields.description: Creator member's {@link hrm_platform_members.id}. Tracks which authenticated member created this task for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Task title or name. Required field that identifies the work item.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the task work. Optional field providing additional context.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current task status tracking workflow progression. Valid values depend on task status workflow configuration.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Task priority classification for work ordering. Valid values defined in priority classification business rules.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Optional due date when the task should be completed. Used for planning and deadline tracking.

plainFields.name: estimated_hours
plainFields.description: Optional estimated hours representing anticipated time required to complete the task. Used for effort planning and capacity management.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was soft deleted. Null means task is active.

models.name: hrm_platform_task_histories
models.description:
Immutable audit trail recording all task status changes throughout the task lifecycle.

Each time a task's status is modified, a new history entry is automatically created to document the transition. This ensures complete visibility into how tasks progress from creation through completion.

The history record preserves the exact moment when a status change occurred and identifies which member performed the modification. Both the previous status and the new status are captured to show the complete transition path.

TaskHistory entries are read-only once created. They serve as factual records that cannot be altered or deleted, providing an accurate account of task evolution. This audit capability supports accountability and helps organizations understand how work flows through their processes.

Key relationships:
- {@link hrm_platform_tasks} - Parent task that this history entry belongs to
- {@link hrm_platform_members} - Member who made the status change

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_task_id
foreignFields.description: Belonged task's {@link hrm_platform_tasks.id}. Each history entry is associated with exactly one task.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_member_id
foreignFields.description: Member who made the status change's {@link hrm_platform_members.id}. Identifies which user performed the modification for accountability.

plainFields.name: old_status
plainFields.description: The task status before the change occurred. Preserves the previous state for complete transition tracking.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: The task status after the change occurred. Records the new state that the task transitioned to.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the status change occurred. Records the exact date and time of the modification.

models.name: hrm_platform_task_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of task records for audit trail and historical tracking.

This table captures the complete state of tasks at specific moments in time, preserving all task attributes including title, description, status, priority, assignment, due date, estimated hours, and temporal fields. Each snapshot is created when significant changes occur to a task, enabling organizations to review historical task states and recover from unintended modifications.

Key relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_platform_tasks} - the parent task being snapshot
- References {@link hrm_platform_projects} - the project containing the task (denormalized)
- References {@link hrm_platform_employees} - the employee assigned to the task (denormalized, optional)
- References {@link hrm_platform_tasks} as parent - for subtask relationships (denormalized, optional)
- References {@link hrm_platform_member_sessions} - the session that created the original task (denormalized, optional)

Snapshots are immutable once created and serve as the authoritative record of task state at a given point in time. They support compliance requirements, audit trails, and data recovery operations.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_task_id
foreignFields.description: Parent task's {@link hrm_platform_tasks.id} that this snapshot captures.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_project_id
foreignFields.description: Project's {@link hrm_platform_projects.id} containing the task at snapshot time (denormalized).

foreignFields.name: assigned_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Assigned employee's {@link hrm_platform_employees.id} at snapshot time (denormalized, optional).

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_task_parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent task's {@link hrm_platform_tasks.id} if this is a subtask (denormalized, optional).

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_member_session_id
foreignFields.description: Creator session's {@link hrm_platform_member_sessions.id} that created the original task (denormalized, optional).

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Task title at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Task description at the time of snapshot (optional).

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Task status at the time of snapshot (e.g., todo, in_progress, done, cancelled).

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Task priority at the time of snapshot (e.g., low, medium, high, urgent).

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Task due date at the time of snapshot (optional).

plainFields.name: estimated_hours
plainFields.description: Estimated hours for task completion at the time of snapshot (optional).

plainFields.name: task_created_at
plainFields.description: Original task creation timestamp at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Task last update timestamp at the time of snapshot.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Task soft delete timestamp at the time of snapshot (null if not deleted).

plainFields.name: snapshot_created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

models.name: hrm_platform_timers
models.description: Active timer sessions for live time tracking. Each timer represents a real-time work session where an employee tracks time as they work. Only one timer can be active per employee at any time. The timer records when work started and when it stopped, with automatic duration calculation upon completion. Timers are always associated with a project and optionally with a specific task within that project. When stopped, the timer can be converted to a timelog entry for permanent record-keeping.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee who owns this timer session. Only one active timer allowed per employee at any time. {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_project_id
foreignFields.description: Project against which time is being tracked. Required for all timer sessions. {@link hrm_platform_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_task_id
foreignFields.description: Optional specific task within the project. Allows granular time tracking against individual work items. {@link hrm_platform_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description of work being performed during this timer session.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timer was started and began tracking time.

plainFields.name: stopped_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timer was stopped. Null while timer is actively running.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp for audit trail preservation.

models.name: hrm_platform_timelogs
models.description:
Individual time entries recording work performed by employees on specific calendar dates.

Each timelog captures a single day's work with duration in minutes, project association, optional task reference, and billable classification. Timelogs serve as the fundamental unit of time tracking, aggregating into weekly timesheets for approval and payroll processing.

Key characteristics:
- Date represents when work was performed and is immutable once created
- Duration recorded in minutes for precise time tracking
- Project association is required; task association is optional
- Billable flag defaults to true for client chargeable work
- Timelogs become immutable once included in approved timesheets
- Soft delete support allows recovery before timesheet approval

Related entities:
- {@link hrm_platform_employees} - Employee who created the timelog
- {@link hrm_platform_projects} - Project the work belongs to
- {@link hrm_platform_tasks} - Optional specific task within the project
- {@link hrm_platform_timesheets} - Weekly aggregation containing multiple timelogs

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee who created this timelog. {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_project_id
foreignFields.description: Project this timelog belongs to. Required association. {@link hrm_platform_projects.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_task_id
foreignFields.description: Optional specific task within the project. Must belong to same project as project_id. {@link hrm_platform_tasks.id}

plainFields.name: date
plainFields.description: Calendar date when work was performed. Immutable once timelog is created.

plainFields.name: duration
plainFields.description: Work duration in minutes. Must be a positive integer value.

plainFields.name: billable
plainFields.description: Whether this time entry is billable to client. Defaults to true for chargeable work.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional text description of work accomplished during this time entry.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timelog was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timelog was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null indicates active timelog.

models.name: hrm_platform_timesheets
models.description:
Weekly timesheet aggregations that consolidate all timelogs for a specific employee within a single calendar week (Monday to Sunday).

Timesheets serve as the official record of work hours for approval and compensation purposes. Each timesheet aggregates timelogs belonging to an employee for a specific week and progresses through an approval workflow with distinct status states: draft, submitted, approved, and rejected.

Key business rules:
- One timesheet per employee per week in submitted or approved status
- Timesheets automatically include all timelogs for the specified week
- Approved timesheets lock all contained timelogs from modification
- Rejected timesheets return to draft status with rejection reason preserved
- Total hours are calculated from included timelogs

Related entities:
- {@link hrm_platform_employees} - Employee who owns the timesheet
- {@link hrm_platform_timelogs} - Individual time entries aggregated in the timesheet
- {@link hrm_platform_timesheet_snapshots} - Historical snapshots for audit trail

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Employee who owns this timesheet. {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: approver_id
foreignFields.description: Employee who approved or rejected this timesheet. {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}

plainFields.name: week_start_date
plainFields.description: Monday date marking the start of the week covered by this timesheet. The timesheet covers Monday through Sunday of this week.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the timesheet in the approval workflow. Valid values: draft (initial state, editable), submitted (awaiting approval), approved (finalized, timelogs locked), rejected (returned to draft with reason).

plainFields.name: total_hours
plainFields.description: Total hours worked during the week, calculated by summing all timelog durations included in this timesheet. Displayed as decimal hours (e.g., 40.5 for 40 hours 30 minutes).

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the employee submitted this timesheet for approval. Null for draft or rejected timesheets.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet was approved by an authorized reviewer. Null for draft, submitted, or rejected timesheets.

plainFields.name: rejected_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the timesheet was rejected by an authorized reviewer. Null for draft, submitted, or approved timesheets.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Reason provided by the reviewer when rejecting the timesheet. Required when rejecting. Visible to the employee for corrections.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timesheet was first created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timesheet was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timesheet was soft deleted. Null means the timesheet is active.

models.name: hrm_platform_timesheet_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of timesheet records for audit trail and historical tracking.

This table preserves the complete state of timesheets at specific moments in time, enabling compliance auditing, historical analysis, and recovery of past timesheet states. Each snapshot captures all timesheet attributes including employee assignment, week period, approval status, approval/rejection details, and total hours worked.

Snapshots are created when timesheets undergo significant state changes such as submission, approval, or rejection. The snapshot mechanism ensures that historical timesheet data remains immutable and accessible even after the original timesheet is modified or deleted.

Key relationships:
- References {@link hrm_platform_timesheets} as the parent timesheet being snapshot
- References {@link hrm_platform_employees} for the employee who owns the timesheet
- Optionally references {@link hrm_platform_employees} for approver information

This snapshot table follows the standard pattern used across the platform for audit trail preservation, similar to {@link hrm_platform_employee_snapshots}, {@link hrm_platform_contract_snapshots}, and {@link hrm_platform_project_snapshots}.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_timesheet_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent timesheet that was snapshot. {@link hrm_platform_timesheets.id}

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_employee_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the employee who owns this timesheet. {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: approver_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the employee who approved this timesheet, if approved. {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}

foreignFields.name: rejected_by_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the employee who rejected this timesheet, if rejected. {@link hrm_platform_employees.id}

plainFields.name: week_start_date
plainFields.description: The start date (Monday) of the week covered by this timesheet snapshot.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: The approval status of the timesheet at snapshot time. Valid values: 'pending', 'submitted', 'approved', 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: total_hours
plainFields.description: The total sum of all timelog durations in hours for this timesheet at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: submitted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the timesheet was submitted for approval, if status is 'submitted' or beyond. Null for 'pending' status.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the timesheet was approved, if status is 'approved'. Null for other statuses.

plainFields.name: rejected_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the timesheet was rejected, if status is 'rejected'. Null for other statuses.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the approver when rejecting the timesheet. Null if not rejected.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the original timesheet was soft deleted. Null if timesheet is active.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this snapshot was created, recording when the timesheet state was captured.

models.name: hrm_platform_activity_logs
models.description: Comprehensive audit trail recording all significant business actions across the organization including employee management events, contract changes, project lifecycle events, task status updates, timesheet approvals, and role assignments. Each log entry is immutable once created and includes the acting user, target entity, action type, and detailed change information for full audit compliance.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_organization_id
foreignFields.description: Organization that this activity belongs to for multi-tenancy isolation.

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_member_id
foreignFields.description: User who performed the action that triggered this activity log entry.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Type of action performed, e.g., 'employee_hired', 'timesheet_approved', 'project_archived'. Used for filtering and categorization.

plainFields.name: target_entity_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity affected by the action, e.g., 'employee', 'project', 'task', 'timesheet'. Used to identify what business object was modified.

plainFields.name: target_entity_id
plainFields.description: ID of the entity affected by the action. Nullable for organization-wide actions not tied to a specific entity.

plainFields.name: action_description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of the action for audit trail clarity.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address of the client when the action was performed, for security auditing.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: HTTP User-Agent header from the request that triggered this action.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this action was performed.

models.name: hrm_platform_activity_log_changes
models.description:
Atomic key-value pairs storing field-level changes for activity log entries.

This table decomposes the changes data from parent {@link hrm_platform_activity_logs} to maintain First Normal Form (1NF) compliance by avoiding JSON storage in string fields. Each record represents a single field change within an activity log entry, capturing the field name, previous value, new value, and field type.

Key characteristics:
- Child table of {@link hrm_platform_activity_logs} with 1:N relationship
- Immutable audit trail data - never updated or deleted after creation
- Managed exclusively through parent activity log operations
- Enables granular change tracking for compliance and history purposes

Use cases:
- Track which specific fields changed in employee records, contracts, projects, or tasks
- Preserve old and new values for audit trail
- Support compliance requirements for detailed change history
- Enable recovery of historical field values

foreignFields.name: hrm_platform_activity_log_id
foreignFields.description: Parent activity log entry's {@link hrm_platform_activity_logs.id}. This foreign key establishes the relationship between the change record and its parent activity log entry.

plainFields.name: field_name
plainFields.description: Name of the field that changed (e.g., 'status', 'title', 'assigned_to', 'end_date'). This identifies which specific attribute was modified in the target entity.

plainFields.name: old_value
plainFields.description: Previous value of the field before the change. Nullable for newly created fields that had no prior value.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: New value of the field after the change. Nullable for deleted fields or when a value is removed.

plainFields.name: field_type
plainFields.description: Data type of the changed field (e.g., 'string', 'int', 'datetime', 'boolean', 'uuid'). Provides context for interpreting the old and new values.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this change record was created. Immutable for audit trail integrity.
